persons with schizophrenia spectrum disorder tend to cope with stressful events in an avoidant manner and that this tendency is associated with both neurocognitive deficits (i.e., visual and verbal memory, executive dysfunction) and certain personality traits (i.e., neuroticism, extroversion).
neurocognitive deficits (especially memory) and personality (especially neuroticism) are associated with avoidant coping in schizophrenia.

neurocognitive deficits (particularly executive function deficits and verbal memory impairments) and neuroticism were related to coping style, whereas extroversion was associated with social support seeking.

the relationship between coping style and neurocognitive deficits in schizophrenia.
the relationship of coping styles and cognitive deficits in schizophrenia.
the role of coping style in schizophrenia and the factors that may influence the development and expression of coping strategies in persons with schizophrenia.

the neurocognitive and personality factors are related to coping strategies in schizophrenia.
the results of this study are consistent with the notion that neurocognition is a key variable that affects psychosocial functioning in persons with schizophrenia.
the neurocognition and the personality of a person with schizophrenia are both independently associated with their coping style.

neurocognitive and personality factors are independently related to coping in schizophrenia.
neurocognition is an important factor in the development of coping style in schizophrenia and that personality factors are not as important as previously thought.

the neurocognition and psychosocial factors that contribute to psychosocial dysfunction in schizophrenia are not mutually exclusive.
